## About

I'm a Researcher in Economic History at Lund University, where I defended my PhD in June 2026. **I study how innovation emerges and who gets to innovate.**

In my research I build large-scale patent and inventor microdata to explain the gender patenting gap, trace how collaboration reshapes inventors' careers, and measure the diffusion of ideas. I develop machine-learning pipelines to turn historical records, including handwritten ones, into data I can analyze.

For more, see my [research](research/index.qmd), [talks](talks.qmd), [teaching](teaching.qmd), [dissertation](https://portal.research.lu.se/en/publications/pins-and-pistons-gender-and-patenting-during-the-french-industria/), and [CV](Youssouf_Merouani_shortCV.pdf).

<p></p>

## Featured Paper

**What Happens When Inventors Collaborate? Evidence from 19th-Century French Patents**
Merouani, Y. 2026. [[Draft PDF]](research/working_papers/Merouani-Patent-Collaboration-Networks.pdf)
*Winner of the 2026 Best Young Researcher Paper Award, International Joseph A. Schumpeter Society.*

Using text-based measures of novelty and influence and Sun–Abraham event studies on the full universe of French patents, I show that collaboration does not raise productivity or originality, but it permanently diversifies inventors' technological focus. I also use network analysis to show that "structural holes" enable this boundary-crossing, with particularly strong effects for women inventors.

<p></p>
